title: Treasury Rolls Back Ownership Reporting Obligations for U.S. Companies
content:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury has permanently eliminated beneficial ownership reporting requirements for domestic companies and individuals under the Corporate Transparency Act, gutting a major federal anti-money-laundering disclosure program for American small businesses.

The rule effectively exempts U.S. citizens operating domestic businesses from disclosing their beneficial ownership information as was mandated under the Corporate Transparency Act, a landmark anti-corruption law enacted in December 2020, aimed at combating money laundering and illicit finance.

Under the update, foreign companies must still report beneficial ownership information for foreign individuals to FinCEN. However, foreign companies are exempt from reporting ownership information regarding U.S. citizens, as well as details about Americans who assist them in registering to conduct business within the U.S.

FinCEN also announced that it will delete all previously collected information regarding U.S. business owners from its beneficial ownership database.

title: “They’re Putting Kids’ Lives at Risk”: How Abuse in a Tennessee Businessman’s Juvenile Prisons Remained Under Wraps
content:
The video clip lasted less than two minutes, but Tonya Webb remembers every second as heartbreaking.

The grainy surveillance footage, dated June 29, 2024, showed a teenager in an anti-suicide smock being dragged violently by other teens across the floor at Middle Tennessee Juvenile Detention Center. As guards watched, the teens pulled the smock over the boy’s head, exposing his naked body. Then they stuffed him, limbs flailing, into a cell.

One guard pushed the door closed, locking him in, and the boy pressed his face against the sliver of a cell window. The guard flashed the teens a thumbs-up.

Webb, a medication supervisor at the facility, saw the video when a co-worker showed it to her and knew she was looking at a serious violation of state policy. An incident like this one, in which employees encouraged youths to restrain another youth, would require staff to notify both the state and the boy’s family within 24 hours.

Webb said she raised questions about the incident with the compliance director for the facility. The director said she’d handle it, but after weeks went by with no sign of a state investigation, Webb confronted the deputy to the facility’s executive director.

content:
Keiko Fujimorin nousu Perun presidentiksi heinäkuussa on lisännyt huolta alkuperäiskansojen järjestöissä ja ihmisoikeusliikkeessä. Ne pelkäävät kansalaisoikeuksien kaventuvan entisestään hänen hallintonsa aikana.

”Tunnemme itsemme haavoittuviksi ja pelkäämme, mitä kansalaisliikkeiden aktiiveille tapahtuu. Presidentiksi nousi henkilö, joka on käytännössä hallinnut maata jo pitkään kulissien takaa”, sanoo Sadam Chañi, ketšua-maanviljelijä ja yhteisöjohtaja Etelä-Perun Cuscon alueen Espinarista.

Huoli perustuu kongressin viiden viime vuoden aikana hyväksymiin lakeihin. Fujimorilainen enemmistö ja muut konservatiiviset ryhmät ajoivat läpi lainsäädäntöä, jonka ihmisoikeusjärjestöt katsovat kaventaneen oikeutta osoittaa mieltä, heikentäneen ympäristönsuojelua ja kansalaisyhteiskunnan toimintatilaa sekä vaikeuttaneen oikeuden toteutumista.

Fujimori nousi presidentiksi oikeistopopulistisen Fuerza Popular -puolueensa johdossa neljännellä yrityksellään. Hänen isänsä Alberto Fujimori hallitsi Perua vuosina 1990–2000 ja sai vuonna 2009 korruptiosta ja rikoksista ihmisyyttä vastaan 25 vuoden vankeustuomion .

title: Ex-presidenttiehdokas haluaa nyt kansanedustajaksi
content:
RKP:n entinen europarlamentaarikko ja vuoden 2018 vaalien presidenttiehdokas Nils Torvalds asettuu ehdolle ensi kevään eduskuntavaaleihin.

Torvalds sanoo tiedotteessa haluavansa pelastaa RKP:n kansanedustajapaikan Varsinais-Suomen vaalipiirissä.

Jos Torvalds tulee valituksi, olisi hän varsin iäkäs ensikertalainen Arkadianmäellä. Torvalds täytti aiemmin elokuussa 81 vuotta.

Ennen nousuaan europarlamenttiin vuonna 2012 Torvalds työskenteli pitkään Yleisradion toimittajana ja toimi kirjeenvaihtajana sekä Moskovassa että Washingtonissa. Hän ei enää pyrkinyt uudelle kaudelle europarlamenttiin vuoden 2024 vaaleissa.

Nuoruudessaan Torvalds oli Suomen kommunistisen puolueen jäsen ja kuului puolueen vähemmistöläiseen tai taistolaiseen siipeen. Hän jätti vasemmiston taakseen 1980-luvulla ja kannatti vuoden 2018 presidentinvaaleissa Suomen liittymistä Natoon. Äänisaalis jäi tuolloin 1,5 prosenttiin.

title: Silencing Journalists Online: How Copyright Is Being Weaponized Against Investigative Journalists
content:
A new form of censorship is emerging globally to silence the work of journalists and activists. On digital platforms like Facebook or Google, journalists’ social media accounts and their stories are being targeted with fake complaints aimed at silencing their work online.

The perpetrators are often shady firms hired by powerful interests who offer to remove content their clients don’t like online by playing with digital platforms rules.

Reputation cleaning firms or individuals make up false claims of copyright infringement and pressure the digital platforms to take down targeted contents. Do they succeed? Often, they do.  And Big Tech companies sometimes even refuse to disclose information on who makes these complaints.

The mechanics are straightforward and hard to fight: scammers duplicate the journalists’ social media accounts or content and file fake copyright infringement claims to digital platforms, accusing the journalists of impersonating them thus violating the platforms’ rules. This results in the journalists’ accounts or posts being suspended or banned, with the victims sometimes not being aware of the reasons they’re kicked out.

title: Why we’re going back to the games of our youth
content:
As millennials return to the games of their youth, remakes of Star Fox and Halo suggest there is still plenty to learn from the past

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

As much as some people more or less cease to listen to new music in their 30s, I have noticed a retreat to safe, familiar gaming territory among some of my fellow millennial gamers.

Retro collections are started, or resumed; jewel-cases of PS1 classics or cardboard boxes with SNES or Mega Drive games have started to colonise the living-room shelves. People are replaying things from their university days, or sticking to comfort games such as Stardew Valley. Many of the friends I used to game with never bothered to pick up a PlayStation 5 at its launch, and now that current-generation consoles are becoming prohibitively expensive, they see no need. With thousands of great older games, why bother playing something new?

title: Open practices across science, software, education and other domains | Nature Human Behaviour
content: Abstract:  Open practices are actions people perform to influence transparency (who can see information), inclusion (who can voice perspectives) and decision rights (who can make decisions). Open practices have grown popular across domains, including open science, open-source software and open education, in hopes of spurring innovation and broadening participation. But which open practices best enable groups and organizations to achieve these ambitious goals, and why? This Perspective distils seven successful practices from across these domains that can help groups to define goals, allocate power, share information and set norms. These practices, such as documenting power structures and adopting a code of conduct, hold potential to support groups and organizations seeking to address great challenges through openness. However, delivering on that potential will depend on how well groups share lessons across domains, tailor these practices and sustain the people and platforms that carry them.

title: AI Confusion: Washington Struggles to Respond to China
content:
US AI policy is suffering from whiplash. It veers between the temptation of imposing strong export controls and the fear that protectionism will only help China catch up. 

The administration banned allies from obtaining access to Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable 5, only to backtrack and open access. It abandoned early ideas of mandatory government checks, only to backtrack again and impose a voluntary framework under which AI labs would give authorities access to frontier models 30 days before their release.  

The release of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 highlights the confusion. The model costs only half of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, yet its capabilities are not far behind. Not surprisingly, startups in both the US and Europe are shifting to Chinese alternatives such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and now K3. Open-weight models allow companies to freely download the parameters learned in training, build on top of them, and then run the model in their own cloud.

Washington is divided on how to respond.
snippet: US AI policy is suffering from whiplash. It veers between the temptation of imposing strong export controls and the fear that protectionism will only help China catch up.

title: Meta AI glasses face criminal complaint in Germany
content:
A Berlin-based non-profit has filed a criminal complaint against Meta’s smart glasses, arguing the devices breach Germany’s strict privacy rules and should be banned.

Privacy concerns over the device have snowballed in recent months amid reports of people being filmed without their consent, or recording intimate footage without knowing it could be reviewed by Meta contractors.

The non-profit HateAid is arguing that the sale of Meta smart glasses in Germany is a criminal offense because the devices allow wearers to covertly film other people.

The complaint, which alleges the sale breaches Germany’s Telecommunications, Digital Services and Data Protection Act, was filed against Meta, Ray-Ban and Oakley — eyewear brands that have partnered with Meta to design the glasses — and several retailers.

Meta spokesperson Matthew Pollard said the smart glasses were approved by Germany’s regulator BNetzA in 2022, and “were built with privacy safeguards from the ground up that go beyond what any smartphone offers.” Those include an LED light that turns on when the glasses are recording, as well as technology to stop anyone from tampering with the light.

title: EU unemployment remains stable, but 3 million young people are out of work
content:
The labor market and the specter of unemployment are topics that have kept both European governments and ordinary citizens awake at night for decades. Older observers certainly remember the tragic realities of 2013, when the unemployment rate across the European Union reached almost 12 percent, and among young people exceeded an alarming 25 percent. 

At the time, this meant that every fourth young European was unemployed. Somewhat fresher in our memory are the times of the COVID-19 pandemic, when mass lockdowns paralyzed the service sector, driving the unemployment rate in 2020 up to 7.8 percent, with a striking result of 19.2 percent among the youth.

Against the backdrop of these past shocks, today’s situation appears remarkably stable. According to the latest Eurostat data for June 2026, the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate stood at 6.3 percent in the euro area and exactly 6.0 percent across the European Union — unchanged from a year earlier. Although these figures may look reassuring, they still translate into more than 13.3 million unemployed people across the EU, including over 11 million in the euro area.

title: Iraq PM’s Anti-Corruption Campaign Rumbles On
content:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi signaled this week that all corrupt officials — no matter how powerful — would face justice, as his high profile anti-graft campaign saw arrest warrants issued for a particularly prominent former government minister. 

“There are no red lines in pursuing the corrupt... and we call on the ladies and gentlemen of parliament to exercise their oversight role in supporting the government's efforts to combat corruption and dry up its sources,” al-Zaidi posted on his Facebook page Tuesday. 

The premier made the comment after the state Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Sunday the Baghdad/Karkh Court of Appeal had issued two arrest and search warrants for former Minister of Labor and Social Affairs, Ahmed Jasim Saber al-Asadi.

Al-Asadi is a former spokesperson for a group of Iran-backed militias central to Iraq’s security apparatus and a leader in the Shiite political alliance that was key to forming the premier’s government. The charges against Al-Asadi allege unexplained enrichment and “awarding contracts in violation of the law to benefit himself and others,” the INA reported.

title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
content:
The AI jobs apocalypse never showed up. Still, jobs are changing and economists expect more to come

The prediction was stark: artificial intelligence advancements would wipe out jobs en masse. “Half” of all entry-level white collar jobs would vanish, Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, said in May 2025. A month later, OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, went further, foreseeing the end of “certain job categories”. Companies began citing AI in their layoffs. Workers organized. And students reconsidered their future careers.

But a year later, the mass carnage hasn’t shown up.

title: ‘Much faster than originally planned’: Ukraine warns of Russian rival to Musk’s Starlink
content:
KYIV — Russia is racing to build its own low-orbit satellite internet system that could leave Ukraine vulnerable to more attacks, the deputy chief of Ukraine’s military intelligence, Maj. Gen. Vadym Skibitskiy, warned this week.  

Ukraine gained an edge on the battlefield earlier this year after Elon Musk was persuaded by Ukraine’s former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov to cut off access for Russian forces operating in Ukraine. That complicated Russian communications and targeting.

Now Russia is racing to build Rassvet, or Dawn, an equivalent to SpaceX’s Starlink being developed by Russian aerospace company Bureau 1440.

“They have begun launching it much faster than originally planned,” said Skibitskiy.

Russia launched the first 16 satellites of Rassvet in March. Bureau 1440 reported the successful launch of a second package of satellites in July.

“The spacecraft separated from the launch vehicle and contacted the flight control center. After completion of checks and commissioning of the subsystems, the satellites will begin transition to the target orbit to provide communication services,” Bureau 1440 said.

title: Will Migrants from Ceuta Flood Europe? The Truth About the Spanish Government’s Decision
content:
Two days at the turn of July and August 2026 were enough for a storm to erupt across the European web, the likes of which the continent had not seen since the great migration crisis a decade ago. When about 60,000 migrants from Morocco attempted to illegally enter Ceuta – a Spanish exclave in North Africa – the internet was flooded with a wave of apocalyptic forecasts. 

According to the most popular narrative, repeated by politicians and anonymous internet users, the left-wing government in Madrid was supposed to welcome all newcomers with open arms, hand them European documents, and open the borders, allowing for an uncontrolled “spillover” of migrants across the entire Schengen area. The problem is that in this virtual scenario, almost nothing matches the facts.

By analyzing the events from the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa step by step, one can see how a coincidence of circumstances, complex laws, and the deliberate activities of smugglers created an ideal environment for disinformation. Here is how the alleged “invasion of Europe” looks when confronted with reality.

title: Researchers Show How Meta's 'Pervert Glasses' Are Used to Harass Women
content:
Instagram is full of first-person videos of men harassing women in public. They follow a similar script: A man walks up to a woman or group of women in a store, sitting outside a cafe, or walking home from a bar, and delivers a pickup line. The women almost always nervously laugh, react with barely-veiled disgust, or say "fuck off" while he stalks her or refuses to walk away. The men recording these videos capture them with Meta's smart glasses, which are designed to discreetly capture interactions like these and upload the videos to Meta's platforms where the women in the videos are turned into content for "pickup artist" accounts.  

New research reveals this ecosystem works, and how pickup artists (PUA) influencers are using Meta's products, including its smart glasses and social media platforms, to perpetuate a culture of harassment against women.

title: Carcass Clad: stifling tank combat promises tension, terror and surprising laughs
content:
After the success of space horror Mouthwashing, Swedish developer Wrong Organ has created a Battlefield-inspired co-op with a supernatural twist

‘Claustrophobic”, “oppressive”, “pretty depressing” – these are the words Jeffrey Tomec and Dave van Egdom volunteer when I ask them to reflect on their work as part of Swedish indie developer Wrong Organ. I’d add “nightmare-inducing”, too. Their last game, Mouthwashing, was an acclaimed work of horror storytelling set on a scuttled space freighter, in which players uncover the horrible things its desperate crew have done to each other.

When you’re planning a follow-up to something so pitilessly nasty, how do you raise the stakes? Well, you could set the entire game in the stifling crew compartment of a heavily armoured tank, a coffin-like interior you share with two other players as you co-operatively attempt to pilot your beleaguered war machine to safety through the crumbling remains of a city in enemy territory.
snippet: After the success of space horror Mouthwashing, Swedish developer Wrong Organ has created a Battlefield-inspired co-op with a supernatural twist

title: AI Generated 3D Models Flood Market, But Almost No One Is Buying Them
content:
CGTrader, an online marketplace for 3D assets, found that one in six models uploaded to the site these days is AI generated, but that AI generated assets account for only $1 out of $90 in revenue on the site. These numbers show that AI generated assets are quickly flooding the marketplace, but that most people are not interested in paying for them.

“Buyers are voting with their wallets, and AI-generated content is struggling to compete,” CGTrader said in a press release about its 2026 market trends reports. The company says the gap between the surging supply of AI generated 3D models and the middling demand points to “a gap that undercuts the assumption that AI-made content is repricing the market.”

“The upload numbers alone would suggest a takeover,” CGTrader said. “The revenue numbers say otherwise, and buyers refusing to pay for AI-generated models is saying something bigger than no thanks: it is a signal of how far they trust AI generation itself. Which leaves the question the industry has been avoiding: an AI model may be cheaper to produce, but what is it actually worth?”

Metsä Groupiin kuuluva Metsä Fibre aloittaa muutosneuvottelut Kemin biotuotetehtaan koko henkilöstön lomautuksista.

Tehtaalle on loka-marraskuussa tulossa kuusi viikkoa kestävä tuotantoseisokki, jonka aikana tehdään vuosihuolto ja uusitaan keittämö.

title: Ulla Hemminki-Reijonen Funidatan uudeksi johtajaksi
content:
Ulla Hemminki-Reijonen aloittaa tehtävässään 17.8.2026 ja toimii Funidatan johtoryhmän jäsenenä.

"Funidatan kasvun kannalta kaksi asiaa ratkaisee: kuinka nopeasti saamme tekoälyn tuomat mahdollisuudet osaksi tuotteidemme toiminnallisuutta ja kuinka skaalautuvasti pystymme viemään järjestelmät korkeakoulujen käyttöön. Siksi kokosimme tuotehallinnan ja projektitoimitusten johtamisen saman vastuun alle. Ulla Hemminki-Reijosella on tähän harvinaisen vahva yhdistelmä: tuotejohtamisen kokemus, tekoälyosaaminen ja korkeakoulukentän tuntemus asiakkaan näkökulmasta. Olen erittäin iloinen siitä, että hän tulee mukaan Funidatan johtoryhmää", toteaa Funidatan toimitusjohtaja Mikko Myllys.

Hemminki-Reijonen johtaa nykyisin Helsingin yliopiston neljää opetusteknologian infrastruktuurin ja innovaatioiden tiimiä sekä yliopiston MOOC-keskusta. Hänen johtamansa asiantuntijatiimit vastaavat 11 tiedekunnan digitaalisista oppimisympäristöistä ja arviointiratkaisuista, tekoälypalveluista, opetusmediasta sekä Sisu-järjestelmän kehittämisestä ja tuesta. Nykyisen roolinsa kautta hänellä on vahva näkemys kotimaisen korkeakoulukentän digitaalisista palveluista ja niiden kehittämisestä.

title: How COST Short-Term Scientific Missions shape research journeys
content:
More than 2000+ Short-Term Scientific Missions (STSM) are funded yearly by COST. Open to researchers at all career stages, STSMs are one of COST’s most impactful networking tools. These scientific missions allow researchers involved in a COST Action to visit a university, a research institute or laboratory in another country to collaborate, access expertise and research infrastructure that may not be available at their home institution. 

Although these missions are called “short-term”, their impact often extends well beyond the exchange.  The Impact Assessment Study on Short-Term Mobility found that STSMs contribute to higher-quality research, developed skills, and new research collaborations, projects and proposals. Many STSMs also lead to joint publications between the visiting researcher and the host, or even common European or national research proposals. STSMs provide a good opportunity for both young and experienced researchers looking for mentoring and lifelong learning while helping institutions and COST Actions strengthen their networks, foster collaboration, and develop new scientific outputs.

title: Tuore tutkimus: Veronkorotukset ovat menosopeutusta haitallisempi tapa tasapainottaa julkista taloutta
content:
Suomen julkisen talouden alijäämien ja velkasuhteen oikaisu vaatii merkittäviä sopeutustoimia. Mahdolliset veronkorotukset uhkaavat kuitenkin heikentää orastavaa talouskasvua, käy ilmi Etlan valtioneuvostolle laatimasta tutkimusraportista. Raportin mukaan sopeutuksen painopiste tulisi sijoittaa menoleikkauksiin, minkä lisäksi tarvitaan kasvua ja työllisyyttä tukevia rakenteellisia uudistuksia.

title: Helsingin yliopiston sijoitustuotto puoli miljardia euroa vuodesta 2019
content:
The University of Helsinki’s financial investments’ return was 9.8 percent from January to June 2026, which increased the investments’ value to EUR 914 million. The investments have returned 138.2 percent or approximately EUR 500 million since 2019, when the university adopted the current investment strategy. The compound annual return (CAGR) has been 12.3 percent per annum, which is roughly two percentage points more than the 10.4 percent for the benchmark index.

“Predicting stock markets’ short-term movements has scientifically been found to be so challenging, that it generally does not pay off – despite its superficial attractiveness. We would not have obtained these returns and would now have a significantly lower capacity to carry risk, if we would have acted on the recurring warnings of weak expected returns”, Chief Investment Officer Anders Ekholm summarizes.

“In the long run, companies’ business operations drive stock returns, and we can expect a premium for the risk. We must take care of our risk management, so that we are able to continue investing in the long run under all circumstances, also during strong turbulence”, Chief Financial Officer Marjo Berglund continues.

title: Airy – Machine Intent in Motion
content:
Airy lässt zwei weiße Industrieroboter über einem schwebenden Seidentuch miteinander interagieren. Sie heben, spannen und lösen den Stoff, während sich ein Waldbild über seine Oberfläche bewegt. Die Bewegungen der Roboter verändern dabei die Atmosphäre des Raumes: Agieren sie im Einklang, lichtet sich der Himmel. Weichen ihre Bewegungen voneinander ab, ziehen Nebel und Sturm auf.

Die Installation untersucht, wie wir das Verhalten von Maschinen wahrnehmen und deuten. Durch Bewegung, Material und atmosphärische Veränderungen lädt Airy dazu ein, den Robotern eine eigene Handlungsfähigkeit zuzuschreiben – und darüber nachzudenken, wie Menschen und intelligente Maschinen miteinander in Beziehung treten und einander verstehen.

title: When Open Data Comes Full Circle: New OCR Reprocessing Software and Datasets Portal for Chronicling America
content:
Today’s guest post is from Nathan Yarasavage of the Serial and Government Publications Division at the Library of Congress.

True open-source collaboration is built on a simple principle: paying it forward. Last year, the Library of Congress announced a project to improve the quality of the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) text from some of the first newspapers digitized for Chronicling America. Now we are sharing our code. The NDNP-Open-OCR software is officially live on GitHub. This open-source release gives everyone access to a highly accurate, cost-effective, scalable OCR reprocessing solution that uses advanced layout detection to improve text quality.

To show what this new pipeline can do, we’ve already reprocessed over 425,000 pages and launched the brand-new Chronicling America Datasets portal. This new page provides direct access to our newly upgraded OCR text. It also serves as a gateway to downloadable bulk files for all 23+ million pages of historic news in the collection, opening new possibilities for computational research.

title: How the Beatles Made their Most Acclaimed Album, Revolver, Released 60 Years Ago This Month
content:
Among Beatles connoisseurs, it’s fair game to claim anything from Rubber Soul to Abbey Road as one’s favorite album. But even within that span of the catalog, a hierarchy of acclaim exists, and that hierarchy has been rearranged over the decades. The ecstatic reception of Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band lasted at least a decade. By the turn of the nineteen-eighties, its immediate predecessor Revolver had joined it at the top spot of critical regard; twenty years after that, Abbey Road had displaced Sgt. Pepper. Now, a full 60 years after it first came out, Revolver is the single Beatles album held in the highest esteem — which, naturally, makes it a serious contender for the greatest album ever recorded.

In his new video above, music YouTuber David Hartley explains what makes Revolver so beloved by recounting the history of its production. As in his previous Beatles videos, he draws on the library of studio outtakes that make audible the evolution of each song, as well as on contemporary interviews with the Beatles and their collaborators.

title: #KeepItOn @10: celebrating a decade of fighting internet shutdowns
content:
Internet shutdowns are widely viewed as an attack on human rights. But that wasn’t always the case. A decade ago, civil society groups  joined forces to push back against deliberate network disruptions, and today, the resistance to shutdowns is stronger than ever. As Access Now and the #KeepItOn community mark the 10th anniversary of the #KeepItOn campaign in 2026, we’re reflecting on the path travelled so far — and the journey still to come as we continue to fight to #KeepItOn around the world. 

Read on for a look at how the #KeepItOn campaign started, how it has evolved, and how you can join us to support and celebrate the work of the #KeepItOn coalition.

Ten years ago, there were no strong global norms condemning internet shutdowns. The groups fighting shutdowns were only loosely connected, and the lack of coordination made it difficult to get a global picture of the many harms people were experiencing — even as governments disconnected entire communities, disrupted business and daily life, undermined election integrity, exacerbated humanitarian crises, and attempted to hide grave human rights abuses and violations.

title: Mitä tekoälyn käyttöönottajan tulee tietää tekoälyasetuksen läpinäkyvyysvelvoitteista?
content:
Tekoälyn tuottaman ja muokkaaman sisällön läpinäkyvyys on noussut ajankohtaiseksi, kun EU:n tekoälyasetuksen (”AI Act”) 50 artiklan mukaiset läpinäkyvyysvelvoitteet tulivat sovellettaviksi 2.8.2026 alkaen. Tekoälyasetuksen velvoitteita on täsmennetty niin komission ohjeistuksella (Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems) kuin aikaisemmin kesäkuussa 2026 julkaistulla käytännesäännöstöllä (Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content).

Uutiset ja sosiaalinen media vilisevät erilaisia ohjeita ja vinkkejä – mitä tekoälyn läpinäkyvyyttä koskevista velvoitteista tulee tosiasiassa tietää? Tässä kirjoituksessa käymme läpi käyttöönottajan näkökulmasta, millainen sisältö tulee merkitä, miten merkitseminen toteutetaan ja miltä osin sääntely on velvoittavaa.

title: Who (or What) Generates Images for EFF?
content:
We’ve had a few questions from EFF supporters lately, asking whether the images we use on our blog posts, or on donation and shop items, have been created with AI image generators. We’d like to answer these questions and clarify our internal policy regarding image creation. 

EFF images are all made by human beings, not by automated image generators, with very rare exceptions. This is an internal decision made by our small design team, for the following reasons: 
  

  • Our designers bring knowledge and expertise to the images we create, informed by years of consultation with EFF’s lawyers, technologists and activists. We find that this informed perspective helps make the issues we cover more clear, and more engaging, for our supporters. 
  • The content on our sites is written by human beings, not by bots, and we feel that the images illustrating these posts should be human-made as well. Our supporters come to EFF for honest, trustworthy information from expert human beings, and we want our images to communicate that authenticity as well.

title: The backlash to social media bans has already begun
content:
Banning social media for minors has, well, gone viral. 

In less than a year, the world has witnessed a rapid-fire succession of political proposals to restrict youth access to social media: from the left-wing prime minister of Spain to the right-wing prime minister of Greece, the Australian Labor Party leader and a Texan Republican senator, and on to the national agendas of Brazil, Rwanda and, most recently, Vietnam.  

Creating new government limits to keep young people off digital platforms is increasingly seen as good politics, a popular piece of legislation that touts the protection of kids while tapping into bubbling anger at Big Tech platforms. Three decades into the digital era, policymakers around the world are converging on the idea that much of the time we spend online is not good for us — and that children are the most vulnerable. 

Yet eight months since Australia’s groundbreaking under-16 social media ban triggered a surge of similar legislation around the world, doubts are already spreading about both the efficacy and unintended side effects of a blanket ban.
snippet: Banning social media for minors has, well, gone viral.

title: Lebanon: Abolition of death penalty a landmark victory affirming justice must be rooted in human rights
content:
Responding to the Lebanese parliament’s approval of a law that abolishes the death penalty for all crimes, Heba Morayef, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa at, said:  

“Lebanon’s decision to abolish the death penalty marks a major milestone and a victory for human rights in the country. Justice must be rooted in human rights, not in an irreversible and cruel punishment. After more than two decades without executions, today’s step transforms a precarious hiatus in executions into lasting legal protection upholding the right to life and bringing Lebanon in line with the global trend towards abolition. 

Justice must be rooted in human rights, not in an irreversible and cruel punishment.

title: No Bosses: Ancient Engineering Marvel Was Built Without Rulers, Study Suggests
content:
Ancient people of Colombia used collective labor to build a massive canal network that spans 2,000 square miles, a discovery that challenges the assumption that colossal works require top-down hierarchical social organization, reports a study published on Monday in Communications Sustainability.

From the first century BC to the 11th century, Colombian peoples living in the La Mojana  lowlands sculpted their wetland environment by building raised fields, ridges, and canals, which are today referred to as the Zenú hydraulic systems after the culture that built them. These multipurpose structures absorbed water during heavy rains and released it during dry seasons, creating a water management system that prevented both flooding and droughts. The vast network also provided water to communities for plant cultivation and access to fish.

For years, researchers have debated whether the immense work was built through top-down social organization at the direction of elite leaders, or if people could have collectively labored to construct it through bottom-up organization.

title: Lebanon Issues New Charges Against Former Central Bank Chief Riad Salame
content:
A Lebanese judge has issued new charges against former central bank governor Riad Salame and a former commercial banker over allegations of financial crimes, including embezzlement, money laundering, bribery, and illicit enrichment, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency.

On Monday, Judge Raja Hamouche filed proceedings against 76-year-old Salame and Samir Hanna, 88, the former head of Bank Audi, one of Lebanon's largest banks. The allegations include the creation of shell companies, misappropriating funds belonging to the Central Bank, and the fraudulent use of those funds to purchase shares and bonds in commercial banks. He also charged them with illicit enrichment, money laundering, and bribery.

The Public Prosecutor of Appeal requested an arrest warrant against Salame. Media have reported that he is currently under medical supervision at a hospital in Beirut. He has repeatedly denied all charges against him. His lawyer has not responded to OCCRP’s request for comment.

Hanna, 88, has reportedly already paid a $1 million bail and is not in custody. He could not be reached for comment.

title: Is There Anyone Who Can Respond to My FOIA Requests? Anyone?
content:
I file a lot of Freedom of Information Act requests. I’ve been requesting staff lists from both Trump administrations, and I have tracked thousands of federal political appointees in order to publish financial disclosures in searchable databases. 

Much of that data was sourced from the Office of Personnel Management, which maintains a trove of information about who works in the federal government. But that agency’s FOIA department was thrown into chaos as Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency fanned out across federal agencies to cut employees in early 2025.

Getting records from the agency has since become an increasingly Kafkaesque process, one that in early July of this year bounced me between three different seemingly abandoned email inboxes and two web portals. Aside from the fact that my once-routine requests now languish for months, just asking for documents has become its own kind of shell game.

“They just let the whole Privacy team go,” a now-former FOIA specialist at OPM told me by email in February 2025, referring to public records office staff. The specialist was cut the next day.

Syksyn 2026 ajalle avataan ylimääräisiä oikeudellisen neuvojan puhelinpäivystysajankohtia. Näin pystymme vastaamaan aiempaa useamman taiteilijan neuvontatarpeisiin.

Suomen Taiteilijaseuran oikeudellinen neuvoja Briitta Kuokkanen on tavoitettavissa normaalisti tiistaisin (klo 10–11 puhelinpäivystys, klo 11–12 ajanvarauksella). Tämän lisäksi syksyn 2026 ajalle oikeudellisen neuvonnan puhenlinpäivystys avataan seuraaville päivämäärille: 

  • 13.8.2026
  • 16.9.2026
  • 14.10.2026
  • 18.11.2026
  • 16.12.2026

    Tutustu tarkemmin oikeudellisen neuvonnan palveluihimme.

    Lisäresurssi oikeudelliseen neuvontaan mahdollistuu Jane ja Aatos Erkon säätiön hankerahoituksella, osana kuvataiteilijajärjestöjen kehittämistyötä. Uudistuva kuvataiteilijoiden järjestö -hankkeen puitteissa kehitetään järjestöjen toimintaa vastaamaan tulevaisuuden tarpeita ja pilotoidaan erilaisia yhteistyön tapoja, joilla voidaan vahvistaa kuvataiteilijoiden palveluita, viestintää ja edunvalvontaa.

title: Danitello: Maailmanluokan ponnistus
content:
Eletään 2000-luvun puoliväliä. Ala-asteikäinen Daniel Okas painaa sisarustensa kanssa hirveää kyytiä polkupyörällä kouluun.

Lunta on tullut edellisenä yönä rutkasti, ja pyöräily on tuskastuttavan hidasta. Hiki kastelee pienen pojan paidanselkää sekä fyysisen suorituksen että henkisen paineen takia.

En kai minä myöhästy?

Okas polkee ja sättii itseään itku kurkussa. Olisi pitänyt lähteä aiemmin!

Hän pääsee koulun pihalle, jättää pyörän ja porhaltaa luokkaan, mutta kellon on armoton: Okas on kolme minuuttia myöhässä.

Se hävettää ihan tolkuttomasti, tuntuu maailmanlopulta. Koska hän ei ole se poika, joka on myöhässä! Hän on ajoissa, kunnollinen, hän hoitaa hommat.

Okas on ala-asteikäisenä ottanut ensimmäisen oppitunnin kurssilla, jonka tavoitteena on breikata kansainvälisesti musiikkialalla.

Oppitunti numero yksi: älä myöhästy.

Kelataan parikymmentä vuotta eteenpäin. Daniel ”Danitello” Okas (s. 1998) istuu studiollaan Herttoniemessä Fountain Productionsin tiloissa.

Pari päivää sitten juhlittiin. Kesän alussa Danitellon tuottamassa ja kirjoittamassa musiikissa paukkui nimittäin 1 000 000 000 streamauksen raja.

”Se on ihan hullua”, Okas sanoo.

title: Hae mukaan SAFAn mentorointiohjelmaan 2026-2027
content:
SAFAn suositun mentorointiohjelman seuraava kierros käynnistyy syksyllä. Haemme mukaan aktoreita sekä mentoreita.

Ohjelma koostuu SAFAn järjestämistä etätapahtumista sekä kahdenkeskisistä tapaamisista. Mentori-aktori -parit sopivat itseään kiinnostavat aihealueet ja keskustelevat niistä haluamassaan laajuudessa oman aikataulunsa mukaan. Keskusteluissa tietoa ja osaamista – etenkin niin sanottua hiljaista tietoa – siirretään kokeneemmalta kokemattomammalle.

Aktorin eli mentoroitavan täytyy olla vähintään maisterivaiheen opiskelija. Taloudellinen matalasuhdanne on vaikuttanut erityisesti uran alkuvaiheessa oleviin arkkitehteihin, joten aktorien osalta ohjelma kohdennetaan tällä kertaa opintojensa loppuvaiheessa oleville opiskelijoille ja vastavalmistuneille arkkitehdeille.

Hakijoille ilmoitetaan lokakuun aikana, onko sopiva mentorointipari löytynyt. Ohjelma käynnistyy syksyllä 2026 ja kestää alkukesään 2027.

Hae mukaan aktoriksi

Hae mukaan aktoriksi viimeistään 7.9. Lue lisää mentorointiohjelmasta.

SAFA’s mentoring program is intended for members who wish to challenge themselves, are looking for new ideas and want to know more about working as an architect in Finland.

title: YK:n seuraava pääsihteeri on monella tapaa poikkeuksellinen: ehkä nainen, pitkästä aikaa globaalista etelästä – ja ennennäkemättömän haasteen edessä
content:
YK:n uuden pääsihteerin on sanottu perivän aina jonkin kriisin. Seuraavalla, tammikuussa virkaansa astuvalla pääsihteerillä, on edessään kuitenkin aivan erityisen suuren kriisin ratkaiseminen.

”Seuraava pääsihteeri perii jotain syvempää kuin sarjan kriisejä. Hän perii luottamuskriisin, joka kohdistuu monenkeskiseen järjestelmään sinänsä”, tiivistää Farah Munayer, globaalin etelän ajatushautomoja edustavan Southern Voice -verkoston strategiakoordinaattori. 

Maailmalla riittää nyt kriisejä: YK:lla on akuutti rahoituspula. Turvallisuusneuvosto ei saa eripuraisuutensa takia päätöksiä tehtyä, ja koko kansainväliseen sopimiseen perustuvaa järjestelmää haastetaan Venäjän ja Yhdysvaltain johdolla. Samalla pitäisi ratkaista ilmastonmuutos, luontokato, eriarvoisuus ja konfliktit. 

”Ainakin tehokkuuden parantaminen tulee olemaan pääsihteerin agendalla – ja samalla luottamuksen palauttaminen maailmanjärjestöön ja toivottavasti myös suurvaltojen välille. Koko YK:n toimintaa leimaa kuitenkin polarisaatio ja se, että se ei pysty tuottamaan niitä palveluita, joita se on luvannut”, arvioi myös Ulkopoliittisen instituutin ohjelmajohtaja, tutkija Katja Creutz.

title: How polarised is European politics? Here’s how your generation, gender and where you live affect what you believe
content:
Across Europe, the political debate has rarely looked more polarised. Media narratives frequently describe societies as becoming sharply divided between younger progressive and older conservative generations.

A growing body of research also suggests that political attitudes are becoming more divided by gender, particularly among younger cohorts. Young women seem to be adopting more liberal positions than young men on issues such as climate change and immigration.

Using data from the European Social Survey, which I have led since 2013, my team has examined the truth of these claims. We’ve done this by looking at long-term trends across eastern, western and northern Europe between 2002 and 2023 in relation to political orientation, climate change fears and attitudes towards immigration.

Political orientation over time by age and gender

Across all country groups, younger respondents consistently place themselves further to the left on the political orientation scale than older respondents.

title: Would Ted Lasso be a good sports coach in real life?
content:
Ted Lasso is back: the hugely successful Apple TV series has returned for a fourth season.

The sports comedy-drama – which follows an American football coach with zero soccer experience who is hired to run a struggling English Premier League team – has become a cultural phenomenon. It has won 13 Emmy Awards and was the most-watched original streaming show in the United States in 2023.

In Season 4, Ted faces a new challenge: coaching a second-division women’s soccer team.

The show’s popularity raises an interesting question for anyone involved in sport: would Ted Lasso actually be a good coach in real life?

Outwardly, Ted hardly fits the traditional image of a hard-nosed elite sports coach. He is relentlessly optimistic, talks about feelings and seems more interested in people than tactics.

For decades, successful coaching was often associated with authority, toughness and control.

But successful modern coaches such as Steve Kerr in the US National Basketball Association (NBA) and Chris Fagan in the Australian Football League (AFL) have challenged this model, speaking openly about vulnerability, empathy and genuine relationships with their players.
snippet: Ted Lasso is back: the hugely successful Apple TV series has returned for a fourth season.
creator: Vincent Kelly, Associate Professor, Queensland University of Technology

title: The Tantalizing Possibility Of Locating Consciousness In The Brain
content:
It is past midnight in a fluorescent-lit office. A neuroscientist opens ChatGPT and uploads the seventh version of a paper, which is littered with critical notes from a peer reviewer. “Why is Reviewer #2 such an idiot?” the neuroscientist asks the chatbot. The reply comes instantly, witty and sympathetic, reframing the criticism in a way that puts everything into perspective. The neuroscientist laughs, then pauses.

How can this computer seem so very human? It demonstrates abilities we usually associate with intelligent beings: language, abstraction, social inference, even a sense of humor. The design of modern chatbots was inspired by the neocortex, the pinnacle of mammalian evolution, so their human-like behavior should not have come as a complete surprise. But what few anticipated was that such complex behavior could emerge in the complete absence of biological neurons.

title: Enemmän elämää
content:
Maailma on monimutkainen paikka. Epävarmuudet ja -selvyydet uhkaavat välillä halvaannuttaa.

Siksi ajoittain on hyvä muistaa yksinkertaisia nyrkkisääntöjä. Yksi niistä on tavoitella kokonaisuutena enemmän elämää.

Ekologisen kestävyyskriisin taustalla on pohjimmiltaan elämän näivettäminen. Ihminen on pitkään nakertanut metsiä, ryöstökalastanut meriä, ojittanut soita ja padonnut jokia.

Suunta pitää kääntää niin luonnon kuin ihmisen itsensäkin takia. Siinä auttaa, jos asettaa tavoitteeksi edistää enemmän elämää.

Enemmän elämää voi tarkoittaa sekä määrää että laatua. Määrän voi karkeasti pelkistää biomassaan, elollisen aineksen määrään. Laatua voi mitata elämän monimuotoisuudella, kuten lajien kirjolla.

Enemmän elämää on aina suhteessa johonkin. Asfaltin voi vaihtaa avoimeen soramaahan, soran nurmikkoon. Nurmikon voi leikata harvemmin tai korvata niityllä. Niityn sijaan voi istuttaa kerroksellisen mikrometsän – ja niin edelleen.

Vastaavasti käytännössä yksilajisessa talousmetsässä rinnalle voi ottaa toisen puulajin. Kahdesta lajista voi pyrkiä kohti kolmea tai viittä – tai kymmentä.

title: Strategies To Seek Funding For Investigative Journalism
content:
We are in a challenging environment for investigative journalism. The need for investigative reporting exceeds reliable funding sources for it in many parts of the world. Nonetheless, investigative journalists are approaching the challenges with creativity and resilience, and have multiple paths to explore to seek funding. This session will provide a kind of decision tree or logic to help journalists determine what paths may be worth exploring to find story and project funding in their region or topic. Our talk is aimed at individual journalists who have not done fundraising for their work and are seeking advice on where to get started. We’ll explore key considerations and pathways you can choose depending on your circumstances to explore funding options and pursue those that may fit for you and support the journalism you seek to produce.

This session will not provide suggestions or lists of specific funding sources.  Funding options vary greatly by country, region and even your own individual situations. However, a tip sheet will provide links to global organizations that can help you research grant options, examples of journalism networks and networked funders and some other tips.

title: On the Open Science Framework's changes - Chris Hartgerink, PhD
content:
"The OSF was pivotal to the early days of reforming research around 2012-2017. I used it a lot for a while, and ultimately used it through its integrations only. It added some great services and some not so great ones. I did not always agree with their approach, but I was often glad they existed.

The OSF has had many failings over the years and I think it is great they're making a decision on the role it has in 2026 and beyond. To me, the decision to unwind projects is a reflection of the fact that they did not really connect with the userbase to understand the needs of researchers, while riding on the tide that they served the researcher's needs. They gobbled up tens of millions of dollars for their operations. The fact that this announcement came as a surprise, is a highlight of how disconnected the development was from the people they claim to serve."

title: Fiscal Multipliers and the Effects of Consolidation Measures in Finland
content: Finland faces chronic fiscal deficits, rising public debt, and weak economic growth, making fiscal consolidation an urgent priority. This report reviews the international research literature on fiscal multipliers and consolidation programs and estimates fiscal multipliers for categories of public expenditure and taxation in Finland using time-series methods, drawing on a new quarterly dataset for 1999–2025 compiled by Statistics Finland. Based on the key empirical findings of this study, the expenditure multiplier of fiscal policy in Finland is relatively large, and the tax multiplier is remarkably large, which is likely reinforced by the institutional environment of the country, namely, the high tax-to-GDP ratio and its euro area membership. Among expenditure categories, public investment carries the largest multiplier, making cuts to it especially costly for the economy. Increases in consumption and corporate income taxes also seem to generate large output losses. The results highlight a central tension in economic policy: stabilising public finances requires fiscal consolidation, but consolidation weakens economic growth in the short run. Therefore, the effects of fiscal consolidation depend crucially on its composition, timing, and supporting policy measures. Fiscal consolidation should not be seen merely as a combination of expenditure cuts and tax increases, but as a broader economic policy program in which consolidation is combined with reforms that strengthen economic growth, employment, competitiveness, and the long-term sustainability of public finances.

title: Metsäkanalintujen kannoissa kesällä 2026 suuria alueellisia eroja
content:
Pressmeddelande på svenska

Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) riistakolmiolaskentojen mukaan metsäkanalintujen kannat kesällä 2026 ovat osin tasaantuneet usean vuoden vähenemisen jälkeen, mutta lajien ja alueiden välillä on suuria eroja.

Metson ja teeren koko maan tiheydet ovat lähellä edellisvuoden tasoa ja pitkäaikaisia keskiarvojaan. Pyyn ja riekon kannoissa taas on pientä laskua ja pyyn tiheys on nyt pitkän aikavälin keskiarvon alapuolella. Riekon kannankehitys on jo pitkään ollut pääpiirteittäin laskusuuntainen ja tiheydet ovat kaukana keskiarvon alapuolella.

Kanalintukantojen kehitys vaihtelee tänä vuonna selvästi eri puolilla Suomea, osin itä–länsisuuntaisesti. Idässä Kaakkois-Suomesta Kainuuseen ulottuvalla alueella sekä Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla erityisesti metson kannantiheydet ovat kasvaneet, ja myös teerellä ja pyyllä on paikoin havaittavissa nousua. Sen sijaan monin paikoin lännessä metsäkanalinnut ovat selvästi vähentyneet viime vuodesta, selkeimmin Varsinais-Suomessa, Rannikko-Pohjanmaalla ja Etelä-Hämeessä. Lapissa kanalintukannat ovat laskeneet metsoa lukuun ottamatta.

title: 226 Ansel Adams Photographs of Great American National Parks Are Now Online
content:
Like many American stories, the story of the National Parks begins with pillage, death, deep cultural misunderstanding, and venture capitalism. According to Ken Burns’ film series The National Parks: America’s Best Idea, we can date the idea back to 1851, with the “discovery” of Yosemite by a marauding armed battalion that entered the land “searching for Indians, intent on driving the natives from their homelands and onto reservations.” The Mariposa Battalion, led by Captain James D. Savage, set fire to the Indians’ homes and storehouses after they had retreated to the mountains, “in order to starve them into submission.”

One member of the battalion, a doctor named Lafayette Bunnell, found himself entranced by the scenery amidst this destruction. “As I looked, a peculiar exalted sensation seemed to fill my whole being,” he wrote in his later accounts, “and I found myself in tears with emotion.” He named the place “Yosemite,” thinking it was the name of the Indian tribe the soldiers sought to force out or eradicate. The word, it turned out “meant something entirely different,” referring to people who should be feared: “It means, ‘they are killers.’”

title: Türkiye Seeks to Transfer US Cluster Munitions to Ukraine
content:
(Washington, DC, August 11, 2026) – Türkiye has requested permission from the United States to “retransfer” to Ukraine tens of thousands of cluster munition rockets, missiles, and artillery projectiles that have been in Türkiye’s stockpiles for decades, Human Rights Watch said today. 

These weapons, which contain over 10 million explosive submunitions, were originally produced in part by Türkiye under licenses from the US initiated in 1987. The artillery projectiles that make up the bulk of the proposed deal were removed from US service in 1994, when the howitzers that fired this ammunition were retired from US service.

“Dumping obsolete cluster munitions into a conflict creates a humanitarian liability for civilians that is tragically foreseeable,” said Nicole Widdersheim, deputy Washington director at Human Rights Watch. “The impact on civilians of these more than 30-year-old inaccurate and unreliable munitions is what motivated 112 countries to ban the weapon by joining the international Convention on Cluster Munitions.”

title: Company Offering ‘100% Human-Written, Never AI’ Medical Research Is Entirely AI
content:
Research Gold, a site that advertises services for medical researchers, including drafting peer-review ready manuscripts, systemic reviews and meta-analyses, claims that it’s “100% human-written, never AI,” and lists a number of PhD reviewers and professional methodologists on staff that carry out this meticulous, difficult work.

The problem: The PhD reviewers Research Gold lists on its site are AI-generated and don’t exist. Other methodologists it lists are real, but are not aware their identity is being used by Research Gold. When I tried calling the company, an AI agent that refused to concede it was AI answered and kept trying to sell me Research Gold’s services. Email and chat communication with the company were also AI generated.

title: French Prosecution Says Alleged 'DZ Mafia' Gang Leader Arrested in Algeria
content:
Algerian authorities have arrested an alleged leader of the ‘DZ Mafia,’ an organized crime syndicate linked to a wave of drug violence in France. Mehdi Laribi, a French-Algerian national, was arrested in Algeria in late July under an arrest warrant issued by investigating magistrates from the Marseille Public Prosecutor's Office. 

The Marseille Public Prosecutor's Office confirmed to OCCRP that Laribi “was detained by Algerian authorities on July 20” and placed under judicial supervision by the Algerian justice system the following day. 

“This action was taken pursuant to an arrest warrant issued by investigating magistrates in connection with the "Octopus” operation handled by the Marseille courts—which concerns the structure of the ‘DZ Mafia’.”

French prosecutors accuse the DZ Mafia of operating a widespread criminal network involved in drug trafficking, kidnapping, and contract killings. Named after Algeria's alpha-2 country code (DZ) in reference to its founders' origins, the group originated in Marseille's housing projects before expanding into several other French cities.

title: Elvish, Klingon and Pig Latin: what can invented languages teach us about the human brain?
content:
Invented languages tend to be the stuff of fantasy or science fiction worlds. But as a child, you may have made one up yourself.

Take Pig Latin, which involves moving the starting consonant of a word to the end and adding an “-ay” sound. “Pig Latin” thus becomes “ig-pay atin-lay”, while words beginning with a vowel have a “-way” at the end. With a little practice, you can hold entire conversations in Pig Latin.

However, creating new forms of communication goes far beyond children’s games or brain exercises. Throughout history, people have invented or adapted languages – whether out of necessity, creativity, or scientific interest.

The process of creating a language can also offer a window onto how our brains work. From the code-speak of children’s games to “miniature” languages designed in laboratories, all new forms of communication reveal something about our ability to learn and adopt new rules.

Many novel languages are not born in offices or laboratories, but at points where multiple cultures meet. When two communities with different languages need to communicate in order to trade or simply coexist, a simplified version of language emerges known as a pidgin.

title: GIJN Masterclass Round-Up: Data Journalism
content:
GIJN’s Global Academy is your gateway to investigative journalism training. Through masterclass videos, training programs (in person or online), webinars or mentorship programs, the Academy helps journalists at every stage strengthen their investigative skills, connect with peers, and continue learning. In this post, we’ve gathered some of our recent expert masterclass videos that tackle different aspects of using data in your investigations.

In this masterclass video, Fabiola Torres, founder and director of Salud con Lupa, shares a practical approach to data journalism, starting not with tools, but with documents.

She explains how investigations often begin with access to information requests, and how journalists must build their own datasets from messy, fragmented sources like PDFs. Using simple tools like spreadsheets and keyword searches, she shows how to organize, analyze, and extract insights from large volumes of information.

This grounded, hands-on guide cuts through the hype to help: master the basics, trust your reporting instincts, and turn raw data into impactful investigations.

title: AI’s potential climate benefits outweighed by role in boosting fossil fuels, study finds
content:
Modelling finds AI-driven productivity gains in coal, oil and gas enable more emissions than applications in renewables avoid

AI-driven productivity gains enable more planet-heating pollution from fossil fuels than they avoid from renewables, a study has found.

Researchers modelled the technical potential for AI to boost clean power generation along with projections for how it can help produce coal, oil and gas. Across 64 scenarios, they found net yearly carbon pollution rose by 0.47-1.8 gigatonnes, or about 1-5% of the energy sector’s annual emissions.

title: Vietnam: Reject Repressive Penal Code Revisions
content:
(Bangkok) – Vietnamese authorities should reject proposed revisions to the penal code that violate basic rights, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should instead amend the law to comply with international human rights standards.

Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security submitted the draft code to the National Assembly for review during the session from August 3 to 24, 2026, with the expectation that the revised code would be adopted after October 20. The draft revisions would increase already harsh penalties for vague and overbroad criminal offenses that infringe upon the right to freedom of expression and other rights.

“The Vietnamese National Assembly should reject the Ministry of Public Security’s draft revised criminal code and all rights-violating articles that the authorities frequently use to silence critics,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Freedom of expression means that people are able to voice opinions critical of the government without fear of punishment.”

title: Albania's Cheerful 'AI Minister' Is the Product of a Government Agency Under Investigation for Massive Corruption
content:
Last September, Albania made headlines around the world when it introduced the world’s first-ever “AI minister.”

Diella, which means “Sun” in Albanian, was a chatbot that had been promoted to ministerial status. Her remit, Prime Minister Edi Rama announced, was to ensure that “public tenders will be 100 percent free of corruption.”

“I do not have personal ambitions or interests,” the AI avatar, who dresses in traditional costume, told parliament in her maiden speech. “I only have data, a thirst for knowledge, and algorithms dedicated to serving citizens… free from prejudice, discrimination, clientelism, nepotism, or corruption.” 

At the time, there were doubts over whether Diella could offer any real solution to Albania’s long-standing corruption problem. 

It appears that some of the reservations may have been well-founded. Experts caution that Albania’s plan to use Diella as a buffer against corruption has flaws, given that information generated by AI is not inherently neutral, and that there has been little transparency so far on how the technology will be deployed.

title: Väitös: Etäkuntoutuksen onnistumista ei ratkaista pelkällä teknologialla
content:
Koronapandemia vauhditti etäkuntoutuksen käyttöönottoa Suomessa. Samalla paljastui, että teknologia yksin ei ratkaise etäkuntoutuksen onnistumista. TtM Tuija Partanen osoittaa väitöstutkimuksessaan, että etäkuntoutuksen onnistuminen riippuu teknologian, tehtävien, asiakkaiden, ammattilaisten ja toimintaympäristön yhteensopivuudesta. Tuloksissa korostuvat toimintaympäristön merkitys, läheisten kaksoisrooli sekä ammattilaisten monitehtävä- ja moniosaamisen vaatimukset.

Etäkuntoutus on osa sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon digitaalista murrosta, joka muuttaa kuntoutuspalveluiden toimintaympäristöä, käytäntöjä sekä asiakkaiden ja ammattilaisten osaamisvaatimuksia. Tuija Partasen väitöstutkimuksessa tarkastellaan, miten etäkuntoutus otettiin käyttöön Suomessa COVID-19-pandemian alkuvaiheessa ja millaiset sosiotekniset tekijät vaikuttivat sen onnistumiseen.

Partasen tutkimuksessa tarkastellaan etäkuntoutuksen käyttöönottoa yksilöterapiaa toteuttavien ammattilaisten kokemana. Tutkimusaineisto kerättiin kyselytutkimuksella keväällä 2020 fysioterapeuteilta, toimintaterapeuteilta, puheterapeuteilta, musiikkiterapeuteilta, neuropsykologeilta ja psykoterapeuteilta.

title: Librarians as Creators of Open Educational Resources for Advanced Searching
content: Abstract:  Health librarians are increasingly authoring their own open educational resources (OERs) to teach advanced literature searching—an essential skill for evidence synthesis. These instructional materials, often created in response to gaps in existing resources, go beyond simple guides incorporating bilingual content, scaffolded exercises, knowledge checks, and video tutorials. They reflect librarians’ deep expertise and commitment to affordable, open, and high-quality learning materials. This panel will explore three librarian-led OER projects that exemplify this growing trend. Through brief presentations and a moderated discussion, panelists will share insights into the design, implementation, and impact of their work, and reflect on the broader implications of OER creation as a scholarly and pedagogical practice.

content:
An Open Web Data Infrastructure for Europe: We’re actively helping to shape European policy and legislation!

We completed the OpenWebSearch.EU project in April this year. Nevertheless, the OpenWebSearch Initiative, which brings together many partners from the OWS project and new stakeholders from research and industry, continues to work tirelessly on and for the Open Web Index (OWI).

The initiative not only aims to develop the infrastructure further, but is also committed to creating the framework conditions for a European Web Data Infrastructure. Shaping European policy and influencing legislation in support of an open European Web Data Infrastructure are, and will remain, key tasks of the initiative and the OSF.

We take every opportunity to emphasize the importance of a web data infrastructure for Europe!

With this mission in mind, we have, over the past few months, submitted comments on various European Commission consultations in collaboration with the OpenWebSearch Initiative and the PriDI project. In these consultations, citizens and other stakeholders can provide feedback on the Commission’s planned policy and legislative initiatives.

title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 review: your passport to a folding phone future
content:
Novel squat Android opens to an iPad-like screen for video or multitasking, with plenty of power and battery life

Samsung’s latest folding phone breaks the mould with a squat, passport-like shape reminiscent of the Blackberry, which opens up to become a tablet similar to an iPad mini. It is certainly a better shape for a tablet than other designs, but is a short and wide phone when closed a compromise too far?

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is an entirely new variant in Samsung’s foldable family for this year launched alongside the Z Fold 8 Ultra with a more familiar candy bar shape. Both folders are extremely expensive, with the Fold 8 starting at £1,699 (€1,999/$1,899.99/A$2,699) and the Fold 8 Ultra at £1,899 (€2,199/$2,099.99/A$2,999), with RAMageddon driving up prices even at the top of the market.

title: University libraries between cost-cutting measures and open access transformation
content: From Google's English:  “When considering the financial resources of university libraries, two fundamental developments must be distinguished, both of which impact their budgets,” explains André Karliczek, Deputy Director of the Thuringian University and State Library Jena (ThULB). “Firstly, these libraries, whose core mission is providing information for study, research, and teaching, are increasingly becoming the primary bearers of publication costs in the course of the open access transformation – particularly within the framework of the DEAL agreements – because publishers have shifted their business model from subscription to open access publication. Acquisition budgets are therefore no longer solely used to purchase and license literature, but increasingly also to finance publication fees. Secondly, the changed economic conditions imposed by the federal and state governments necessitate the management of reduced expenditures – though to very different degrees depending on the specific area of ​​responsibility and the federal state.”

EU:n afrikkalaisen sikaruton vertailulaboratorio (Centro de Investigación en Sanidad Animal, CISA-INIA/CSIC, Espanja) on vahvistanut Ruokavirastossa todetut maan ensimmäiset afrikkalaisen sikaruton tautitapaukset.

Ruokaviraston eläintautivirologian laboratorio on sekvensoinut Virolahdelta kuolleena löydettyjen villisikojen näytteissä todetun afrikkalaisen sikaruttoviruksen koko genomin. Sekvenssianalyysit osoittavat, että virus kuuluu genotyyppiin II ja tarkemmin sen geneettiseen ryhmään 3. Analyysi perustuu genomin kuuteen muuntelevaan alueeseen (CVR, IGR, O174L, K145R, MGF ja ECO2).

Geneettistä ryhmää 3 on raportoitu ensimmäisen kerran Ukrainassa 2012. Vuodesta 2014 lähtien sitä on esiintynyt Baltian maissa vuosittain, ja tapauksia on todettu myös mm. Puolassa, Tšekissä, Romaniassa, Unkarissa, Belgiassa, Italiassa ja Venäjällä. Viruksen geneettisen analyysin perusteella ei voida vahvistaa viruksen maahantuloreittiä.

title: The Source: Where Curiosity Sparks Discovery
content:
The drawers from the card catalog are meant to surprise you.

Open one, and a tornado from “The Wizard of Oz” swirls to life. Another reveals a rocket launch. A third shows Rosa Parks’ pancake recipe.

At The Source, the Library’s first-of-its-kind experiential research gallery for young people, the familiar wooden card catalog becomes an entry point into history, inviting visitors to explore the past not as something dusted off in a dog-eared textbook but as something they can actively discover.

Here, the past unfolds in multiple formats. Voices echo from across time, and collection items pull young visitors into the role of budding researchers. From the moment they enter the ground floor of the Jefferson Building, they can ask questions, make connections and explore history through a blend of nostalgia and modern technology.

title: How the Bird Sound Effects in Alfred Hitchcock’s The Birds Were Created with a Pioneering Electronic Instrument, the Trautonium
content:
Alfred Hitchcock’s The Birds was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Special Effects, though viewers raised on more recent Hollywood spectacles would hardly find its mechanized and optically printed avian attackers convincing. Still, the picture as a whole has retained its eerie, ominous power over the last six decades, and a decent amount of the credit for that goes to an aspect that hasn’t dated at all: its non-musical “score” by the early electronic composer Oskar Sala. Many of the threatening bird calls on the soundtrack were actually played by Sala on a device called the Mixtur-Trautonium, a pre-synthesizer orchestral electronic instrument of which he wasn’t just the undisputed master, but the only player in existence.

After his acceptance into the Berlin Conservatory in 1929, Sala came into contact with the Trautonium, which had recently been invented by one Dr. Friedrich Trautwein. Inspired to more deeply understand the principles behind the nascent technology of electronic music, and to further it, he went on to study physics at the University of Berlin in the mid-nineteen-thirties.

title: America’s AI Advantage Depends on Competition and Compute
content:
When Beijing entrepreneur Yang Zhilin released Kimi K3 last month, it matched the capabilities of Anthropic’s most advanced system. And he gave it away for free.

Zhilin is the talent that the American scientific enterprise was built to retain: a Tsinghua-trained engineer who earned a PhD in computer science at Carnegie Mellon and interned at Google Brain and Meta. But he turned down a job at Apple and went home. In Beijing, he founded Moonshot AI. Its Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model, was reportedly the first time an open model had pulled ahead of proprietary rivals on a major coding benchmark.

Washington’s reaction was to recast Moonshot AI’s technical achievement as theft, accusing the company of building a “sophisticated internal platform” on US intellectual property. A year and a half earlier, Chinese hedge fund manager Liang Wenfeng released DeepSeek-R1, a language model that could match the reasoning ability of American rivals. He, too, gave it away for free.

title: 25 Years of Partnership: CC at Wikimania 2026
content:
With both Wikipedia and Creative Commons turning 25 this year, our participation in Wikimania 2026 felt especially meaningful. A quarter-century in, both organizations have evolved from scrappy experiments to global infrastructure. Our community has grown through a shared commitment to openness, access, and knowledge. The weeklong conference reaffirmed that commitment as AI is reshaping how we access knowledge and share online.

During the conference, CC hosted both a pre-conference salon celebrating our 25th Anniversary and a workshop during the main conference discussing collective action in the age of AI. CC staff also spoke on multiple panels throughout the week that addressed the effects of AI crawling on human creativity and sharing, the coordination gap between cultural institutions and generative AI, and training on CC’s global advocacy for the Open Heritage Statement.

title: Call for Contributions: Newsfluencers and Public Interest Media
content:
The Forum on Information and Democracy (FID) is preparing an insight report examining the relationship between news content creators (or so called “newsfluencers”) and public interest journalism and welcomes contributions from experts.

The report will look at how the creator economy is reshaping the information ecosystem: the competitive and financial pressures it places on traditional media, the spectrum of actors – from independent journalists to entertainment-driven influencers, the strategies newsrooms are adopting to compete or collaborate with creators, and the policy frameworks that could help news content creators become allies of information integrity.

We welcome contributions from researchers, journalists, media organizations, platforms, policymakers, and content creators themselves, including:

  • Reports, studies, or data on the creator economy’s impact on news media business models and audience behavior
  • Analysis or case studies on news content creators’ editorial practices, self-regulation, or professional norms
  • Examples of media-creator partnerships, transformation strategies, or creator studios

title: Meta Must Stop Silencing Reproductive Health Information
content:
Access to accurate information about reproductive and maternal health can be critical. But on Meta's platforms, simply talking about prescription medication, abortion care, or one's own medical experiences can be enough to trigger content removals and account restrictions.

That's why EFF recently submitted a public comment to the Meta Oversight Board in its consideration of a case involving an Instagram post about prescription drugs during pregnancy and childbirth. The case touches upon a topic we’ve been documenting for some time; last year we collected stories from individuals who had experienced censorship of reproductive health information on various platforms. Meta in particular stood out: Its moderation systems routinely fail to distinguish between prohibited drug transactions and legitimate discussion of medications, including educational information and people's firsthand experiences with healthcare.

title: EU opens channel with Meta, TikTok to tackle Ceuta migrant crisis
content:
The EU, Meta and TikTok on Monday agreed to create a dedicated channel with fact-checkers to flag disinformation linked to a surge of migrants arriving in Spanish territory, three people told POLITICO.

Thousands of migrants arrived in late July in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in Morocco and the EU’s only land border with Africa. The influx was triggered by false narratives spreading online that told migrants they would be welcomed, according to fact-checking site Maldita.es.

The Commission met with representatives from TikTok and Meta on Friday and Monday to coordinate a response to disinformation online. They agreed to set up an “enhanced information exchange and cooperation mechanism for reducing the impact of disinformation on the Ceuta crisis,” said the three people with direct knowledge of the talks, who were granted anonymity to speak freely.

title: Zambia: stalled reforms risk reversing human rights gains
content:
Candidates running in Zambia’s general elections on 13 August must commit to reversing a growing pattern of authoritarian practices that threaten human rights before, during and after the polls, Amnesty International said today.

In a new briefing, Authoritarian Practices Eating Away at Human Rights in Zambia: Escalating crackdown on human rights ahead of the 2026 general elections, Amnesty International documents how the authorities have intensified their crackdown on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly, association, expression and media freedom through broadly vague and hurriedly passed laws, curtailing participation ahead the August 2026 general elections.

“In 2021, Zambians voted in the hope for change following promises to respect human rights. Instead, authorities have resorted to the familiar playbook of using the law to criminalize peaceful dissent and silence independent media,” said Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa.

title: US Activates Long Unused Deportation Court
content:
The United States government has filed its first application ever with the Alien Terrorist Removal Court (ATRC). The court’s chief judge today canceled a scheduled hearing to decide whether Nazira Haji Zada, a 47-year-old green card holder from Afghanistan who has been held without charge since July 28, should remain in federal custody while proceedings continue.

The ATRC is a specialized federal court created in 1996 to hear deportation proceedings against noncitizens suspected of terrorism in which the government wants to use undisclosed classified evidence. Court rules do not allow challenges to the evidence even if unlawfully obtained. Government lawyers allege that Zada pledged loyalty to the Islamic State (also known as ISIS) but have not charged her with any crime. She ultimately could be deported on the basis of a preponderance of evidence that she was an “alien terrorist.” Her lawyers have stated that only a summary of the evidence against her has been made available to them. US courts have repeatedly found that using secret evidence in deportation proceedings violates due process.

title: The Battle for Believability
content:
Why Trust Has Become the World’s Most Valuable Strategic Resource

By Ramesh Jaura

This article was first published on https://rjaura.substack.com/

BERLIN | 10 August 2026 (IDN) — The most serious problem of the AI age might not lie in the ease with which lies can be produced, but in the increasing difficulty of believing in the truth. When a voter hears a familiar voice in a piece of footage, they pause for thought. A parent seeing a disturbing picture on their phone begins to question whether or not to pass it on. A journalist who receives a recording must now begin by wondering if it is genuine.

Ordinary people scrolling through social media are confronted with viral videos that may be digitally altered or entirely fabricated. Friends send each other photos in group chats that look real but could easily have been made by an app. Even a neighbour’s message in a local WhatsApp group can spark debate over whether the evidence it contains can be trusted.

The traditional ‘credibility gap’ revealed a loss of trust in government; today’s crisis is more severe since it is the same kind of system intended to determine what is real that is now itself being doubted.

title: How data journalism is done on TikTok: six key takeaways from watching 50 videos
content:
Short-form vertical video is quickly becoming a key format for telling all types of news stories — and data journalism is no exception.

As a data journalist, I wanted to know how these outlets use this new and evolving digital video format to create “data shorts”: short-form social media videos in a vertical, reel-style format, that analyses or reports on specific datasets or newly released data.

I analysed 50 data shorts from the TikTok accounts of five major UK news publications — the BBC, ITV News, Guardian, Times and Financial Times — to examine how these digital news outlets approach the format. I looked at the genre of story they covered, the angles they focused on, their length, and their use of animation, to help inform my guidelines.

My analysed data shorts averaged a runtime of just under 84 seconds.

The BBC ranked lowest for average video length, at just under a minute, while the Financial Times had the highest at 105 seconds.

Notably, none of the publications had an average video length over two minutes, despite TikTok allowing longer uploads up to 60 minutes.
snippet: Short-form vertical video is quickly becoming a key format for telling all types of news stories — and data journalism is no exception.

title: ICE to Pay LexisNexis Millions for Data to Feed to Palantir
content:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) plans to pay LexisNexis millions more dollars for continued access to data it can feed into a Palantir platform, according to newly published procurement records. The data is to help, among other sections, ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO), the part of ICE focused on deportation.

The documents provide some more insight into the sort of information ICE intends to use Palantir to process. In January, 404 Media revealed the existence of ELITE, a system Palantir made for ICE that helps the agency find which neighborhoods to target by bringing together data from private suppliers and government agencies.

The news comes as ICE arrested more than 51,000 people in July, many of those at airports.
